stem: A Team has Players who OUTLIVE the team and can join others. This is:
explanation: Aggregation: has-a where the part exists independently. The team is GIVEN players it did not create. UML: hollow diamond.

stem: A House and its Rooms - demolish the house, the rooms are gone. This is:
explanation: Composition: the whole OWNS the part; the part cannot outlive it. The House CREATES its rooms. UML: filled diamond on the House end.

stem: In code, the composition/aggregation difference boils down to:
options: Whether the part is CREATED inside or PASSED IN
explanation: _rooms.Add(new Room(...)) = composition. Sign(player) where the player arrived from outside = aggregation. That is the entire distinction.

stem: Printer.Print(Document d) uses the document and keeps no field. This weakest relationship is:
explanation: A passing acquaintance: parameter in, used, forgotten. Weakest coupling and usually the best - if a parameter will do, do not make it a field.

stem: In UML, a HOLLOW TRIANGLE arrowhead pointing at Animal means:
explanation: The hollow triangle is inheritance (solid line) or interface realisation (dashed line), always pointing AT the parent/interface.

options: An order has at most one line
An order has AT LEAST ONE line
explanation: 1..* = one or more. 0..1 = optional single. * = any number. The numbers sit at the end they describe.

stem: In a UML class box, the symbols -, +, # mean:
explanation: - private, + public, # protected; underlining marks static. The three compartments are name, attributes, operations.

stem: The diamond (filled or hollow) sits on which end of the line?
explanation: The diamond marks the owner: House gets the filled diamond, Team the hollow one. The part end carries the multiplicity.

stem: Best general advice when unsure which relationship to use?
options: The WEAKEST relationship that does the job - weaker is easier to change
explanation: Strength ranks roughly: inheritance > composition > aggregation > association > dependency. Prefer the loosest that satisfies the need.

stem: Student knows Teacher AND Teacher lists tutees. The hazard of this bidirectional association?
options: Setting one end and forgetting the other leaves the model inconsistent
explanation: Two ends must be kept in step (AssignTutor updates both). Prefer one-directional links where possible - fewer ways to be wrong.
